institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The choice was a mix of academic oppotunities—studying arctic marine biology in the arctic—and the opportunity to ski, hike, dive, and all outdoor activities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. However, I had classes during the intro day, and they recommended that I attended those, therefore, I missed quite a lot of infomation, but I got the info from other students instead.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I emailed a bit with the exchange coordinater regarding practical stuff

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think the intro days were great for those who could attend. Otherwise, they're were good at helping via email.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Really easy. You just apply for housing through Samskipnaden as soon as possible and I haven't heard about someone not getting student housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Tromsø, everything is close to campus. There are "express" busses to campus from almost all student housing, so it's super easy to get to campus. The crosscountry ski tracks run all the way across the island (Tromsøya) so you can even ski to uni.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very nice, however, a lot of the student housing is not very social, but it depends a lot on which floor you end on.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It wass fairly easy, they have good guides on their webpage that are easy to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always send an email or call or just go to a help desk or their offices at campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got a the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the guides on their webpage

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses corresponded quite well to the level I'm used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes are a lot smaller, so the teachiing is way more intimite and interactive and the teachers know all names. There's a lot more practical teaching such as lab, excursions, cruises etc. There's a lot more hand-ins, reports, and presentations durinng the semester and in generel more requirements to fullfil in order to attend the exams, but also a lot more feedback on our work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: BIO-2010 Marine Ecology, BIO-2513 Marine Biodiversity, BIO-2516 Ocean Climate

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them, but Marine biodiversity was the best overall, however be aware that it's in norwegian, though that wasn't a problem. All of them include a cruise, lab sessions, and marin biodiversitet also has excursions. The teachers are really good.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The bus and housing is really cheap. Outdoor equipment is really expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Basically everything. They have TSI which is a lot of student sports clubs, and every week they send us a very detailed email with everything that is happening during the coming week, and there's a lot. To just mention a few: knitting club, waffle friday, dinners, activities at the museum, the return of the sun event and so much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All kinds of skiing. There's a small alpine park where Samskipnaden have some free tickets you can use, there's a lot of crosscountry ski tracks, and my favourite is Randonee skiing. Diving is also amazing (SUT is the student dive club), participating in Rissa citizen science is also super nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend becoming a member of DNT and get a DNT key you can use for the huts in the area and then go on some hut trips. Get a tent and go hike in the mountains. Go skiing. I don't think there's a need to go on trips far away as everything is accessible just outside your door.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you can—enroll in a course that is taught in Norwegian. Joing one of the TSI groups.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The cultural differences are more or less non-existent. But be aware that sundays and holidays are taken seriously, everything is closed, also supermarkets.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoor environment and the slower pace of everything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Participate in everything you find interesting, explore new activities, get new hobbies.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you struggle with all the practical stuff, just send them an email. I would recommend participating in the intro days, eventhough you have classes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being outdoors, being active, the slow pace and chill environment. The very engaging teaching—I've learned a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Leaving

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
